# CairoDrive — Provider Decision Document

**Date:** 2026-08-05 · **Scope:** which API key serves which capability, and which keys to never register.

---

## 0. Ground truth corrections — read before anything else

Three premises in the brief and in the upstream research are wrong. Everything downstream depends on them.

**0.1 — There are no TomTom or HERE integrations in this repo.** The brief states "there are existing TomTom + HERE traffic raster overlays." Verified false by grep: no `api.tomtom.com`, no `hereapi.com`, no `api.here.com`, no `api.mapbox.com` anywhere in the tree. Every TomTom/HERE mention is a code comment citing competitor behaviour as design rationale (`RouteRecalculationHelper.java:212`, `CairoDriveOffRoute.java:19`), plus three `here.com` hosts in `AndroidManifest.xml:642-644` that are geo-URL deep-link parsing. **There is nothing redundant to drop on the traffic side. This is a greenfield choice, not a de-duplication.**

**0.2 — What actually ships today is a Google traffic overlay on the OSM map.** `GoogleTrafficHelper.java:85` calls `routes.googleapis.com/directions/v2:computeRoutes` with `extraComputations: ["TRAFFIC_ON_POLYLINE"]`, and `GoogleTrafficLayer.java` paints the returned `speedReadingIntervals` as vector geometry onto the OsmAnd GL map (registered `MapLayers.java:147`). Default is off (`OsmandSettings.java:3436`, `GOOGLE_TRAFFIC_ON_ROUTE = false`). This is a **worse** ToS fact pattern than the Places pin — Google routing content drawn as map geometry on a non-Google basemap, squarely §19.2.

**0.3 — Four of the five "deferred" Places features are already written.** `GooglePlacesDetailsApi.java:80-83` implements Place Details, Autocomplete, Nearby Search and Photos. Build-flag defaults in `cairodrive.gradle:457-472`:

| Flag | Default | Console quota (per CLAUDE.md) |
|---|---|---|
| `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_DETAILS` | **`true`** — shipping now | 32/day |
| `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_PHOTOS` | `false` | 50/day |
| `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_REVIEWS` | `false` | — |
| `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_AUTOCOMPLETE` | `false` | 32/day |
| `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_NEARBY` | `false` | **0 — hard blocked** |

So "shipping a Places feature" is a flag flip plus a console quota raise, not an integration. That changes the build order completely.

**0.4 — Verification status.** Only three sources were readable in the research sessions: Google's ToS and Service Specific Terms (`cloud.google.com`), Microsoft's Azure Maps transaction docs (raw GitHub), and OSM's `settings.yml` (raw GitHub). Every other provider's pricing and licence text is recollection, not a reading. Anything not from those three is tagged **[UNVERIFIED]** below. The Google ToS clauses quoted here are verbatim and confirmed.

**0.5 — The one legal fact that governs the whole stack.** Google Maps Platform ToS §3.2.3(e): *"Customer will not use the Google Maps Core Services with or near a non-Google Map… For example, Customer will not (i) display or use Places content on a non-Google Map."* Repeated per-service: Places §14.2, Routes §19.2, Roads §17.2, Geocoding §6.2. Note the shape — §14.1 explicitly permits use with **no** map; only use with **another** map is forbidden. There is exactly one override in the entire agreement, §15.1 Places UI Kit: *"…with or without any map, including a non-Google Map. This clause will prevail over the No Use with Non-Google Maps clause."* UI Kit is an Android View/Compose widget, so it does not survive a plain HTTP client and will not render inside Android Auto templates. **There is no compliant way to put a Google pin on your OSM map on the car screen.** No private-use, internal-testing or non-commercial exception exists anywhere in either document.

That is a fact, not advice. What you do with it is your call — the practical exposure at ~12 requests/day is key suspension, not litigation. The rest of this document assumes you keep Google for search with eyes open, and buys everything else from providers that do not have that clause.

| Capability | Winner | Runner-up | Why the winner | Free-tier headroom |

Google's Cairo data is better and is the one thing §19.2 names | Tile bucket 50,000 **[UNIT UNVERIFIED — day vs month post-Orbis]**. A 45-min drive at z14-16 ≈ 440 tiles |
| **Traffic incidents** | **TomTom** `incidentDetails` (JSON, bbox) | HERE `/v7/incidents` | One bbox call covers the whole corridor. `fields` selector trims payload for the data saver; `t` traffic-model-ID detects "nothing changed"; `categoryFilter=6,7,10` = lane closure, road closure, flooding. Actionable objects, not pixels | Non-tile 2,500 **[unit unverified]**; ~20 calls per drive |

## 2. What ONLY each provider can give you

The point of this section is that nothing distinctive goes unmilked. Ordered by how much the unique thing is worth here.

**TomTom**
- `confidence` (0-1) per flow segment — a provider telling you how much probe data backs each answer. In Cairo, where Salah Salem and an unnamed alley differ by an order of magnitude in coverage, this is the field that lets you gate ETA correction per-street instead of trusting the whole city equally. Nobody else exposes it.
- `roadClosure` boolean on the same response — the one traffic event that should actually trigger an offline reroute.
- **Split quota buckets.** 50,000 tile requests/day is a *separate* pool from 2,500 non-tile requests/day. Your overlay draws from a pool you cannot exhaust while the scarce pool is reserved for calls that drive logic. No other provider partitions it this way. **[UNIT UNVERIFIED]**
- Snap to Roads returning `speedLimits` + functional road class from a raw GPS trace, on the standard free tier — Google gates the equivalent behind an enterprise Asset Tracking licence.
- `supportingPoints`/`encodedPolyline` reassessment: POST *your* offline route geometry, get a traffic-aware travel time for exactly that path. One transaction, no risk of two routers disagreeing about which roads to take.

**Google**
- The Cairo Places corpus. Arabic + English names, informal and unbranded businesses, side-street POIs the OSM Egypt extract does not contain. This is not replaceable and it is why the key stays despite §14.2.
- Session-based autocomplete: keystrokes cost $0 when the session ends in a Details call. Since `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_DETAILS` is already `true`, that termination already happens.
- Places UI Kit §15.1 — the only written override of the non-Google-map clause anywhere in the agreement. Worth knowing exists; unusable on Android Auto.

**OpenWeather**
- First-class sand/dust condition codes (7xx group) on the **free** current-weather endpoint. Tomorrow.io's `weatherCode` vocabulary has no sand or dust member at all **[UNVERIFIED but load-bearing — settle it with one free key before ever preferring Tomorrow.io]**. For a car driven through khamsin season this single field decides the weather provider.
- Free transparent XYZ tiles on a static URL template (`tile.openweathermap.org/map/{layer}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?appid=`) — drops into OsmAnd's existing overlay machinery as a tile source, no code.
- A dedicated free Air Pollution endpoint with its own quota, no card.

**Open Charge Map**
- Publishes the entire database as a git repo partitioned by ISO country. Egypt is 492 JSON files. **This inverts the integration**: bundle or sync once, then never touch the network. No other POI provider makes a fully-offline layer possible. Verified from the official export at commit 2026-04-22: 311 in Greater Cairo, operators Infinity EV / Sha7en / Elsewedy Plug / TAQA Volt / IKARUS, 482/492 operational, 65 verified during 2026.

**Mapillary**
- Machine-detected traffic signs as queryable geodata, including `regulatory--maximum-speed-limit-*` classes. The only free path to speed-limit data that does not depend on an OSM tag already existing. This feeds a custom Egypt `.obf`, which CD_NARROW already concluded is the only way to act on the signal.
- Street imagery with no basemap-display requirement.

**OpenStreetMap OAuth**
- The only **write-back** channel in the entire provider list. Every other provider is read-only — you consume their errors and they stay broken forever. Notes can be filed anonymously with no OAuth at all; GPX trace upload from a driver who does Cairo daily is the single highest-leverage thing here for the alley-geometry problem.

**Stadia Maps**
- `trace_attributes` returns per-OSM-edge `roadClass`, `laneCount`, `surface`, `unpaved`, `speedLimit`, `wayId`, `tunnel`, `bridge`, `roundabout` for a matched GPS trace. It is a measurement instrument for CD_NARROW that runs on your laptop and touches neither the frame budget nor the battery.

**Azure Maps** (verified figures, dropped anyway — see §4)
- Weather Along Route: up to 60 waypoints each with lat/lon + ETA-minutes + heading, returning a 0-4 hazard index, precipitation dBZ, lightning count, **sun-glare rating computed from your supplied heading**, and notifications for hazards not yet reached. Nothing else has this shape. Egypt is covered.
- The only provider whose billing mechanics I could verify at source: 15 tiles = 1 transaction, Route Matrix = `ceil(0.25 × O × D)`, Snap to Roads = 100 points per transaction, Autocomplete = 10 requests per transaction, **5xx/401/403/408/429 not billed**, and the free allowance is a *standing monthly* allotment, not trial credit.

**HERE**
- `in=corridor:{polyline};r=200` + `locationReferencing=shape` — hand it your offline route, get flow for exactly that corridor with drawable geometry, one request. Elegant, and replicable with TomTom point sampling.

**Mapbox**
- Map Matching with `annotations=congestion` on the driving-traffic profile: your polyline in, per-segment congestion out. The cleanest annotation shape in the whole survey. Killed by billing posture, not by capability.

**Geoapify**
- 20 POIs per credit on category search, and explicit written permission to cache, store and redistribute results — the opposite of everyone else's caching rules.

**Yandex / Magic Lane / LocationIQ / MapTiler / Tomorrow.io / BestTime**
- Nothing unique that is usable here. Details in §4 and §5.

## 3. Combination plays

Concrete pairs, and what each looks like on the head unit at 60 km/h.

**3.1 — TomTom `incidentDetails` → OsmAnd offline reroute.** Poll one bbox around the next ~10 km every 2-3 minutes with `categoryFilter=7,6,10` (road closure, lane closure, flooding). A closure ahead is the only traffic event an offline router structurally *cannot* know and the one that reliably produces a wrong turn. On screen: nothing at all until a closure intersects the route, then a single Android Auto alert card plus an automatic offline recalculation avoiding that segment. ~20 requests per drive. This is the highest-value combination in the document because it changes behaviour rather than colour.

**3.2 — TomTom `flowSegmentData` × OsmAnd's own route → ETA correction.** Sample 5-8 points spaced along the polyline ahead of the vehicle, every 5 minutes. Per segment compute `currentTravelTime / freeFlowTravelTime` and apply the ratio to the offline engine's remaining leg times. **Gate every sample on `confidence`** — discard anything below your measured threshold rather than trusting it, because in Cairo arterial and alley confidence will differ enormously. On screen: the existing ETA field simply becomes right, plus a small "+7 min" delta. 50-80 requests per drive against 2,500. Unlike Google, TomTom's terms do not forbid speaking it, so the delta can go through the Arabic TTS path.

**3.3 — Do NOT run 3.2 and a flow tile overlay in the same build.** Both answer "where is the traffic". CD_FRAME already shows `over` at 25.9 ms / 61% of a 46.9 ms frame, and a raster overlay plus new Java drawing lands in exactly that bucket. Ship the JSON logic first (invisible, no frame cost), and only add the tile layer afterwards, alone, with `avgOver` and `maxMs` read before and after. If the tiles cost you 5 ms, they are not worth it — the number is already the app's main problem.

**3.4 — Sun glare with zero API calls.** Azure's per-waypoint `SunGlare` hazard code is genuinely useful on east-west Cairo arterials at dawn and dusk. It is also fully computable on-device: solar azimuth and elevation from date/time/lat-lon (no network, no data), route bearing from the polyline the offline engine already produced, glare when |azimuth − bearing| is small and elevation is below ~15°. **This replaces the single best reason to register an Azure key.** Build it locally.

**3.5 — Two-of-three dust detection.** OpenWeather current-weather condition code in {731, 751, 761, 771} **OR** PM10:PM2.5 ratio spiking well above baseline (mineral-dust fingerprint) **OR** reported visibility at its floor. Require two of the three to agree before showing anything — a single-signal dust warning will false-positive and the driver will stop trusting the banner. On screen: one persistent amber strip, "Dust — reduced visibility", no audio interrupt. Two calls at trip start plus a refresh every 30 minutes. Both endpoints are free with no card.

**3.6 — Stadia `trace_attributes` + TomTom Snap to Roads on the same recorded trace.** Laptop-side, post-drive, beside `cd-analyze.py`. Stadia gives per-edge `roadClass`/`laneCount`/`surface`/`wayId`; TomTom gives `speedLimits` from a different vendor's map. Diff both against what your `.obf` believed. Output: a per-drive list of edges where OSM has no `maxspeed` but TomTom does, and edges where road class disagrees. That is a measured input to a custom Egypt `.obf` and it is the correct successor to the static CD_NARROW percentages. One transaction per drive per provider. Zero runtime risk.

**3.7 — Mapillary `map_features` → OSM edits via your own OAuth client → `.obf` rebuild.** Query detected `regulatory--maximum-speed-limit-*` points over Cairo, cross-reference against ways with no `maxspeed`, and file OSM Notes (or, at a desk, edits) for the gaps. This is the only loop in the entire provider landscape where driving the car improves the router. Slow, but it compounds and nothing else does.

**3.8 — Google `searchText` for the name, OCM's bundled dataset for the substance** (only if the car is electric). Google finds "the charger at CityStars"; the bundled OCM record supplies operator, connector type, kW, and — critically — that 66% of Egyptian stations are tagged *Public — Membership Required*, so the UI must not promise walk-up access. `UsageCost` is populated on 0.8% of Egypt records, so never display a price.

## 4. Redundant — drop these, do not register the key

| Provider | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **HERE** | **Drop** | Duplicates TomTom on flow and incidents. Its Limited Plan was decommissioned (new customers 2025-03-27, existing 2025-08-31) so a **card is now mandatory and overage is billed, not blocked** — strictly worse than TomTom's card-free freemium **[UNVERIFIED]**. Its two distinctive bits (corridor filter, Browse category search) are replicable with TomTom point sampling and Google Nearby. A Cairo-local comparison rated HERE WeGo traffic notably worse than Google in this city. |
| **Mapbox** | **Drop** | Worst billing posture in the survey: **no user-configurable spending cap** and `pk.` tokens cannot be restricted by package + SHA-1 on Android — Mapbox's own docs say URL restrictions are for GL JS only. That removes both controls that make the `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` decision defensible. Plus Product Terms require Geocoding and POI results be used *"in conjunction with a Mapbox Map."* Its unique Map Matching congestion shape does not buy back an unbounded bill on an extractable token. |
| **Azure Maps** | **Drop** | The traffic/routing/search half is TomTom data resold through Microsoft billing — same Cairo congestion, extra subscription, extra auth, extra bill. The weather half reduces to sun glare, which §3.4 computes offline for free. Card mandatory, overage billed (Budgets are alerts, not caps). **Gen1 pricing tier retires 2026-09-15 — six weeks out — with automatic migration to Gen2 at roughly 9× the per-transaction rate** [tier retirement verified; rate multiple unverified]. Keep one fact in your pocket: Egypt is ticked for *Address points* (rooftop) geocoding in Microsoft's own coverage table, which is unusual for North Africa. |
| **Yandex** | **Drop, and delete inherited code** | No Egypt coverage of anything — no jam scoring (Russia/Türkiye/Kazakhstan only), no panoramas, not in the Navigator routing country list. Free tier requires data be displayed on the Yandex map **and** requires the app be freely downloadable by any internet user, explicitly excluding closed systems — Play internal testing disqualifies you on distribution grounds alone. Separately: this fork inherits `OsmAnd/src/net/osmand/plus/views/YandexTrafficAdapter.java`, which hits the undocumented internal endpoint `core-jams-rdr.maps.yandex.net`. Dormant (needs a tile source with rule `yandex_traffic`, `MapTileLayer.java:200`), unauthorised, useless in Egypt. Remove it. |
| **LocationIQ** | **Drop** | Strictly dominated by Geoapify: 48-hour cache ceiling on the free tier (vs Geoapify's explicit permission to cache and store) collides with the CD_SEARCH prefix cache; 2 rps vs 5 rps punishes any keystroke stream; its Nearby endpoint is BETA with an unstable contract vs Geoapify's 400-800 structured categories at 20 POIs per credit. Its only unique feature is a `/v1/balance` quota endpoint. |
| **MapTiler** | **Drop** | Only satellite imagery is non-redundant, and it is blocked by MapTiler's own client README: *"data fetched from MapTiler Cloud API… cannot be stored or redistributed in any way"* — OsmAnd caches tiles to sqlite by design, so intended use would mean disabling tile caching on a metered link. |
| **Magic Lane** | **Drop** | No REST API exists at all (5,662 files of official Android docs searched, zero HTTP endpoints). Everything runs through their MapView, i.e. their renderer must be what is on screen. It replaces OsmAnd rather than complementing it. |
| **Tomorrow.io** | **Drop** | Free plan is hour-limited at ~25 calls/hour **[UNVERIFIED]** — roughly one call every 2.4 minutes, which cannot support in-drive refresh or multi-waypoint sampling. And its `weatherCode` vocabulary appears to have no sand or dust member, leaving PM10 as the only dust proxy while burning the scarce quota. Uncapped `visibility` (vs OpenWeather's 10 km clamp) is its one real advantage and does not carry the decision. |
| **Geoapify** | **Do not register yet** | Genuinely clean — no basemap clause, no card, caching permitted, and its Places API fills the "petrol near me" slot. But Google Nearby is already *written* in your tree and has far better Cairo POI data. Geoapify is the documented escape hatch if the Google key is ever suspended, not a build. |
| **Stadia Maps** | **Register only for the audit** | Free key, laptop-side only, `trace_attributes` for §3.6. Never in the APK. Its free-tier credit pool number is suspect: the reported 2,500/month yields ~80 tiles/day, which would make its own flagship product unusable — that premise is probably wrong, so do not size anything against it. |
| **BestTime.app** | **One free query, then almost certainly drop** | Register free, run `GET /api/v1/venues/search?q=malls in Cairo`, count the results. Every example in their own repo is US-based. If Cairo comes back empty — the likely outcome — the provider is closed. If it comes back populated, you still have a Play-policy question about shipping scraped Google data. |
| **Google Geocoding, Time Zone, Elevation, Maps Static, Aerial View, Roads, Route Matrix, Route Optimization, Solar, Pollen, Air Quality** | **Never enable** | Redundant with `searchText`/Android/SRTM/`.obf`, or unavailable (Speed Limits is licence-gated; Aerial View is US-only; Egypt is outside Solar coverage), or ToS-restricted to uses you cannot build (Air Quality §2.1 permits only AQ-based *routing* and environmental indices; Solar §20.1 permits only energy-system work). Each one is another SKU, another quota and another surface under §3.2.3(e). |

**Also drop from the tree:** `GoogleTrafficLayer` and the `TRAFFIC_ON_POLYLINE` path in `GoogleTrafficHelper`. It is the clearest §19.2 breach in the codebase, TomTom replaces it cleanly, and leaving dead-but-flippable code behind a preference is how it gets switched on by accident.

**Final key list — hold these, nothing else:**

| Credential | Card? | Where it lives | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` | Yes (existing) | GitHub secret → BuildConfig | Search, details, nearby, autocomplete |
| TomTom API key | No **[UNVERIFIED]** | GitHub secret → BuildConfig | Traffic flow, incidents, ETA correction |
| OpenWeather key (2.5 + Air Pollution only) | No | GitHub secret → BuildConfig | Dust, air quality, weather tiles |
| Mapillary client token — **your own** | No | BuildConfig | Imagery + sign detections |
| OSM OAuth 2.0 client — **your own**, PKCE | No | BuildConfig (no secret needed) | Notes, GPX upload, edits |
| Stadia key | No | Laptop only, never in the APK | Trace-attribute audit |
| Open Charge Map | — | **No key** — data bundled | EV layer (if applicable) |

## 5. Egypt reality check

Plainly, what will disappoint.

**Genuinely good in Cairo**
- **Google Places.** Best by a wide margin. Arabic and English names, informal businesses, alley POIs OSM does not have. This is the whole reason the legal problem is painful rather than academic.
- **Google traffic.** Its float is every Android phone in the city. Best available, and the one you cannot use on your map.
- **TomTom traffic flow.** TomTom publishes a dedicated Cairo Traffic Index city page (2025: 21.1 km/h average, 74 hours lost per driver, up 3h50m YoY). That index is computed from the same floating-car data that feeds the Flow API — direct evidence of real probe density, not a marketing coverage map. Expect it to be strong on arterials and ring roads and thin-to-absent on unnamed alleys.
- **Open Charge Map.** 492 Egypt records contributed by *Egyptian* operators, not mirrored from a Western chain index. 26% offer ≥50 kW DC. Actively maintained into 2026.
- **Azure geocoding.** Ticked for *Address points* (rooftop) in Microsoft's own coverage table — genuinely unusual for North Africa. Noted for the record even though the key is dropped.

**Thin, and it will show**
- **TomTom / HERE incidents.** Incident feeds lean on traffic authorities and press reports. Egypt has far less of that infrastructure than the Netherlands. Expect major closures and roadworks, not the dense incident carpet you see in demos. **Test empirically before building UI on it — one `incidentDetails` bbox over greater Cairo settles it in five minutes.**
- **HERE traffic and POIs.** A Cairo-local navigation-app comparison rated HERE WeGo's traffic notably less accurate than Google here. POI density well below Google.
- **Mapbox, Stadia, Geoapify, LocationIQ, MapTiler search.** All reduce to OSM in Egypt (OpenAddresses has no Egypt corpus; Foursquare's Egypt data is thin and stale). Querying them over the network gets you what your `.obf` already holds locally. Streets yes, alleys poorly, businesses effectively no.
- **Yandex.** Not a market. No jam data, no panoramas, not in the routing country list. Cairo gets the low-detail world basemap, which is worse than your `.obf`.
- **Azure severe weather alerts — verified NOT available in Egypt.** Egypt's row in Microsoft's coverage table is blank in that column, as is every North African country. The endpoint answers; nothing is behind it.
- **Government weather alerts generally** (OpenWeather One Call `alerts`, HERE, Tomorrow.io Events). These require a national met agency publishing machine-readable feeds. Egyptian Meteorological Authority coverage in commercial aggregators is believed absent. Expect empty arrays. **Compute your own thresholds locally instead** — it will be more reliable and costs nothing.
- **Radar-derived products.** OpenWeather One Call `minutely` nowcast, RainViewer, HERE/Azure radar tiles — all radar-driven, and Egypt has effectively no radar coverage. Model-based precipitation tiles render; radar-based ones are blank frames.
- **EV charging as a *feature*.** 492 stations nationwide and **66% tagged membership-required**. Useful if you drive an EV, close to pointless otherwise.
- **Mapillary Cairo coverage — unverified and probably arterials-only.** Sample a few Cairo bboxes before spending a day on the sign-detection pipeline. Detection quality also depends on Egyptian sign styles being represented in the training set, which is unknown.
- **BestTime.app — unverified and most likely empty.** Popular-times data derives from Google Popular Times; thin-coverage countries are exactly where scraped datasets return nothing.
- **Public transit (any provider).** Cairo's network is dominated by informal microbus and shared taxi, which publish no GTFS. Worst-covered thing in the entire survey for this city.
- **Google Solar (Egypt not covered at all), Aerial View (US only), Pollen (desert metropolis).** Dead on arrival.

**One thing to stop expecting**: no provider will fix Cairo's alleys for you. CD_NARROW measured tags at ~2.5% and alley names at ~16.6%, and every commercial provider is either weaker there than OSM or is OSM. The only mechanisms that move that number are §3.6 (measure the gap per drive) and §3.7 (write back to OSM). That is slow and it is also the only real answer.

---

## 6. Cost safety

**Traps, ranked by how much they could cost you.**

1. **Mapbox has no spending cap at all.** Not a low cap — none. Exceeding a free tier sends one courtesy email per billing period and keeps serving; the card is charged when the invoice finalises. Combined with an unrestrictable `pk.` token compiled into the APK, this is the single worst posture in the survey. It is why Mapbox is dropped rather than merely deprioritised. (Note the upstream research contradicts itself on this — one section says billed overage, another says "at times card-free with a hard stop." **[UNVERIFIED]**. It does not matter: the token restriction problem stands either way.)

2. **OpenWeather One Call 3.0 is a subscription, not a free tier.** Payment details are mandatory to subscribe even though the first 1,000 calls/day are free, and the account's default daily call limit is believed to be 2,000/day — so calls 1,001-2,000 **bill silently** rather than 429ing **[UNVERIFIED]**. Mitigation if you ever enable it: set the account daily call limit to exactly 1,000 first, converting it to a hard stop. This is the identical control already applied to `SearchTextRequest` at 160/day, and the same reasoning holds — the quota ceiling is the only bound nothing can forge around. **Recommendation: do not enable One Call at all.** 2.5 Current + 5-day forecast + Air Pollution cover the need with no card and no billing surface.

3. **Trial credit is not a free tier.** Google's $300/90-day Cloud trial and Azure's $200/30-day free-account credit are one-off and expiring. The recurring thing is different: Google's post-March-2025 **per-SKU monthly allotment** (10,000 Essentials / 5,000 Pro / 1,000 Enterprise **[UNVERIFIED]**), and Azure's documented standing per-meter monthly allowance (**verified**: *"you get 5,000 free Base Map Tile transactions per month"*). Never size a decision against a trial number.

4. **Google SKU escalation from one field.** You are billed at the highest tier any requested field belongs to. Adding a single Enterprise field to `GetPlace` — `rating`, `regularOpeningHours`, `internationalPhoneNumber`, `priceLevel` — drops headroom from 5,000/month to 1,000/month in one line of field mask. Exactly the "a change that looks like one line is a change to the bill" case CLAUDE.md already warns about. Audit the current mask in `GooglePlacesDetailsApi.java` before raising any console quota.

5. **Autocomplete is billed per session, not per request.** Keystrokes are $0 **only** when the session terminates in a Details Pro/Enterprise call. An abandoned 8-keystroke session costs ~$0.023, i.e. ~$22.60 per 1,000 abandonments. Two implementation requirements, both mandatory: pass a session token, and always close the session. Since `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_DETAILS=true` already ships, the terminating call exists — wire the token to it. **[UNVERIFIED: whether Autocomplete carries a monthly free allowance like every other SKU. It is the only Google row in the research with no allowance stated, and that omission is not explained. If it does have one, CLAUDE.md's "by far the most expensive here" characterisation is wrong and the 32/day cap is over-conservative. Check the console before deciding.]**

6. **Google Photos are not cacheable.** Places ToS §14.3 permits caching latitude and longitude only, for at most 30 consecutive days. Photo bytes, display names, formatted addresses and types are not cacheable at all. So every photo view is a fresh download on a metered link, and bitmap-heavy fetches surface as GC pauses in CD_FRAME `maxMs` even when the average looks fine. Keep `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_PHOTOS=false`.

7. **Your current search cache is technically offside §14.3, mildly.** `GooglePlacesSearchApi.java:336` stores the whole response body, which includes `displayName` and `formattedAddress` per the field mask at lines 129-130. But it is a static in-memory `LinkedHashMap`, 64 entries, 5-minute TTL (lines 164-165, 873-874), gone on process death. That is the mildest possible form of the violation — nothing persists across sessions. Worth trimming to id + lat/lng on the next touch of that file; not worth a build of its own.

8. **HERE raised pricing ~6% effective 2026-04-01.** That date has passed. Every HERE figure in the research predates it and is stale by construction. Moot given the drop, but relevant if you ever revisit.

9. **TomTom's free-tier unit is unresolved and the difference is ~30×.** The research states 2,500 requests/**day** and 50,000 tiles/**day** in eleven places, while its own analysis notes TomTom restructured around Orbis with a **monthly**-transaction allowance. If it is monthly, every TomTom budget in this document is 30× too generous. **Open `developer.tomtom.com/store/maps-api` and read the two allowances before writing a line of code.** TomTom also revised developer pricing effective July 2026 — a month before today — so all figures are pre-revision.

10. **Do not mix TomTom Orbis and legacy endpoints in one app.** TomTom states this explicitly and it is not boilerplate: different underlying databases, geometries that may not align, non-shared feature identifiers. Commit to one family across tiles, `flowSegmentData` and `incidentDetails` together. Orbis is forward-looking but its Routing v2 drops `sectionType=lanes`, `roadShields`, `tollRoads` and `handsFreeDriving` and restricts `travelMode` to `car`. If lane data ever matters you are on legacy — decide now, because switching later re-does every endpoint.

11. **Attribution is a real obligation on TomTom, and traffic tiles carry no embedded branding.** TomTom's terms require implementing the Copyrights API for services that do not auto-generate a logo. A transparent traffic overlay on your OSM map with no "© TomTom" credit is exactly the case that clause covers. Cheapest compliance item on the list — do it in the same build as the overlay.

12. **Azure does not bill error responses** (5xx, 401, 403, 408, 429, CORS preflight) — verified. Noted because it is the one billing behaviour in this survey that protects you, and nobody else documents an equivalent.

13. **Play Data safety.** Every new provider that receives coordinates is a new third-party recipient under "Location — precise", required on every track including internal testing. TomTom `flowSegmentData` sends a point; `incidentDetails` sends a bbox around where the driver is. OSM GPX upload sends the entire location history. The category does not change from what Places already forced, but the declaration should name the new recipients — re-confirm rather than assume.

14. **Every key ships inside the APK.** TomTom and OpenWeather have no package + SHA-1 equivalent to Google's. For both, the **daily quota cap is the only real control** — set it low at signup, before the key ever ships, exactly as was done for `SearchTextRequest`.

---

## 7. Recommended build order

One feature per build, each judged on a real drive log, ordered by (value to a Cairo driver) ÷ (risk + cost). Steps 0 and 1 are not features and carry no drive-log risk — do them first because they cost nothing and close real footguns.

**Build 0 — Credential hygiene. No user-visible change.**
Register your own Mapillary client token (currently using OsmAnd's hardcoded token at `TileSourceManager.java:40` — heavy use could get *OsmAnd's* token throttled). Register your own OSM OAuth 2.0 client with PKCE and a `cairodrive://` redirect (currently shipping upstream's client id **and plaintext client secret** at `no_translate.xml:70-71`, redirecting via `osmand.net`; `AndroidManifest.xml:575-585` still registers the `osmand-oauth://` scheme, so if real OsmAnd is installed on the POCO C85, Android shows a chooser and your authorization code can land in the other app). Stop proxying Mapillary photos through `osmand.net/api/mapillary/*` (`MapillaryImageDialog.java:73-75`) — go direct to `thumb_*_url`. Delete `GetMapillaryUserAsyncTask` (calls the retired v3 API, can only fail) and `YandexTrafficAdapter`. Compile check on `dev`, no signed run needed.

**Build 1 — Google Nearby Search.** `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_NEARBY=true`, and raise the console quota from **0** (per your own convention, raising the quota *is* shipping the feature). Highest driving utility of anything deferred — "petrol near me" is a thing you want at 60 km/h — one call, no per-keystroke exposure, code already written, no new key, no new attribution. Render results as an Android Auto list rather than pins where you can; it is template-constrained anyway and therefore incidentally further from §14.2's worked example. **Read:** CD_SEARCH request count and cache hit rate, CD_FRAME `over` and `maxMs`.

**Build 2 — TomTom incident alerts.** `incidentDetails`, one bbox over the corridor ahead, poll every 2-3 minutes, `categoryFilter=7,6,10`, `fields` selector trimmed to geometry + category + delay, `t` model-ID for change detection, `language=ar`. A closure or flooding event intersecting the route triggers an alert card and an offline recalculation. This is the first genuinely new capability and the first thing that changes behaviour. **Before writing code:** confirm the free-tier unit (§6.9) and run one bbox call over greater Cairo to see whether Egypt incident data is actually populated — five minutes, and it will tell you more than any coverage table. **Read:** a new CD_TRAFFIC line (request count, HTTP status, incident count, whether a reroute fired), plus CD_FRAME unchanged.

**Build 3 — TomTom ETA correction.** `flowSegmentData` at 5-8 points ahead, every 5 minutes, `confidence`-gated. Log `confidence` and `currentSpeed`/`freeFlowSpeed` per sample from day one — that is the dataset that tells you whether TomTom's Cairo probe density is real on *your* streets or only on Salah Salem. No new map drawing, so no frame-budget exposure. **Read:** CD_TRAFFIC confidence distribution, ETA error against actual arrival, CD_FRAME unchanged (it should be — if `over` moved, something is on the wrong thread).

**Build 4 — Dust and air-quality banner.** OpenWeather 2.5 current + Air Pollution, two-of-three signal agreement per §3.5, one Android Auto strip, no audio. Free, no card, no billing surface. **Read:** how often the banner fires versus how often you actually saw dust — a false-positive rate above roughly one in five means retune the thresholds before keeping it.

**Build 5 — Sun-glare warning, computed locally.** Solar position + route bearing, zero network. Cheap, genuinely useful on east-west arterials at dawn and dusk, and it removes the last reason anyone would register an Azure key. **Read:** CD_FRAME `wdgt` — this is widget-class drawing work and belongs in that bucket.

**Build 6 — TomTom flow tile overlay** (`style=relative-delay`, so only congestion draws). Optional and last of the traffic work, because it is the only piece that competes for the frame budget. Add the Copyrights API attribution in the same build. **Read:** `avgOver`, `maxMs` and `avgMs` before and after, on the same route. If it costs more than a couple of milliseconds, drop it — you already have the traffic information from Build 3, and this only paints it.

**Build 7 — Google Autocomplete.** Last, and alone, because it has the highest regression risk of anything here and it is the specific feature behind the "buggy as hell" incident. Requirements: hard debounce, session token passed **and** closed against the existing `GetPlace` call, and `CAIRODRIVE_PLACES_AUTOCOMPLETE=true` shipped with nothing else. **Judge it while TYPING, not after** — CD_SEARCH cache-hit-rate collapse and CD_FRAME during keystrokes are the whole test.

**Never (unless something changes):** Photos (uncacheable, GC pauses, metered link). Reviews (same field-mask SKU escalation, no driving value). EV charging (unless the car is electric — then it is a one-off bundled dataset, not a build).

**Parallel track, no build slot, no risk — do this alongside everything above.** The trace-attribute audit from §3.6: register a free Stadia key, run one recorded drive's GPX through `trace_attributes` and TomTom Snap to Roads on the laptop, diff both against the `.obf`. Output is a per-drive count of edges missing `maxspeed` and edges where road class disagrees. That replaces the static CD_NARROW percentages with a measured, per-drive number, which is exactly what "measure before optimising" asks for — and it is the only input that makes a custom Egypt `.obf` worth building.
